newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money high, central bank offers repos.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money high, central bank offers repos.

text.p: Jakarta call money was still expensive on Wednesday morning as the central bank extended its policy of keeping short-term rates high, dealers said.
Overnight money eased to 19.0/20.0 percent from an early high of 27.0/28.0 percent.
The central bank kept its interest rates for short-term bilateral papers (SBIs) unchanged on Wednesday and remained absent from the short-term securities (SBPUs) market.
But Bank Indonesia offered 200 billion rupiah of one-week SBI repos at 13.75 percent for Wednesday following the maturity of the same amount of repos available last week.

The bank offered overnight bilateral SBIs at 14.0 percent, two-to-six day at 15.0 percent, one-week at 10.0 percent, two-week at 10.5 percent, one-month at 11.125 percent, three at 11.0, six at 11.625 and one-year at 12.25 percent.
One Japanese bank dealer said liquidity was not really tight but was kept artificially high to make the financing of dollar purchases expensive.
"If you need rupiah there is no problem. It's only expensive. It's not like you want rupiah but there is no offer," the dealer said.
A net balance of 349 billion rupiah was available to the market from the maturing central bank papers on Wednesday.
Dealers said they were not clear how long the policy of expensive short-term rates would proceed, but it would be necessary until the market regained full confidence.
Some said inverse interest rates in the market reflected operators's expectation that the condition was temporary.
One-week money was at 19.0/20.0 percent while one- and three-month money were both at 18.5/19.5 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Tuesday was 21.9 percent, compared with 21.49 percent on Monday.
